clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old healthy donor undergoes a bone marrow evaluation.
morphology_cue_template: Age-appropriate cellularity with granulocytes at all maturation stages.
editor_note: For a normal marrow biopsy, specify why obtained if desired

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old is undergoing a marrow evaluation with otherwise reassuring blood counts.
morphology_cue_template: Cellularity is appropriate for age, with a complete range of granulocytic maturation.
editor_note: Avoid implying all clinically evaluated children are healthy

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old presents with fatigue and bruising; circulating blasts are identified.
morphology_cue_template: Increased blasts with reduced normal granulocytic maturation.
editor_note: Use leukemia classification nuance in parent notes if needed

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old develops pallor and easy bruising, and a blood smear shows blasts.
morphology_cue_template: Blast-rich marrow with reduced normal maturation.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old is evaluated for marked leukocytosis and splenomegaly.
morphology_cue_template: Marked granulocytic proliferation with full maturation and a left shift.
editor_note: BCR::ABL1 confirmation is outside this visual model

clinical_vignette_template: Routine bloodwork in a {age}-year-old reveals persistent neutrophilic leukocytosis.
morphology_cue_template: Hypercellular marrow with increased intermediate granulocytic precursors.
editor_note: The clinical history alone is nonspecific

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old presents with fatigue, infections, and pancytopenia.
morphology_cue_template: Markedly hypocellular marrow with abundant fat spaces.
editor_note: Exclude other causes clinically; marrow appearance alone insufficient

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old with persistent pancytopenia undergoes a bone marrow biopsy.
morphology_cue_template: Very sparse hematopoiesis and extensive fatty replacement.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old undergoes marrow examination two weeks after cytotoxic chemotherapy.
A {age}-year-old receives intensive chemotherapy and has prolonged cytopenias.
morphology_cue_template: Sparse residual marrow cells with prominent fat spaces.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old has rising neutrophil counts following chemotherapy.
morphology_cue_template: Regenerating marrow with increased immature granulocytic forms.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old is recovering blood counts after a period of marrow suppression.
morphology_cue_template: Granulocytic maturation is returning, often with a left shift.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old recently received filgrastim after chemotherapy.
morphology_cue_template: Granulocytic hyperplasia and a left shift, consistent with growth-factor effect.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old receives pegfilgrastim as supportive care during cancer treatment.
morphology_cue_template: Expanded granulopoiesis with abundant maturing precursors.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old with recurrent bacterial infections is evaluated for severe persistent neutropenia.
morphology_cue_template: Granulocytic maturation is reduced beyond the promyelocyte/myelocyte stage.

clinical_vignette_template: A {age}-year-old has recurrent infections and profound neutropenia from early childhood.
morphology_cue_template: Early granulocytic precursors predominate, with few mature forms.
